Synopsis:
The Beetaloo shale gas basin in northern Australia has achieved its first gas flow milestone, amid a geopolitical energy security crisis triggered by a US-Israel aerial campaign against Iran (starting Feb 28, 2026) that has disrupted Strait of Hormuz traffic. Qatar's LNG exports have effectively collapsed, spiking spot LNG prices to $25.80/MMBtu (+150% vs. pre-war levels). This has accelerated interest in Australian LNG as a secure, chokepoint-free alternative for Asian buyers. Major players (Inpex, Santos) are now active in Beetaloo alongside smaller operators. With Asian gas demand projected to grow ~30% over the next decade, Beetaloo's 200 tcf recoverable reserves position it as a strategically significant long-term supply source, contingent on infrastructure build-out.
